correctness.rationale: PASS — For each d≥3 and fixed positive P,Q,B, the reduced weighted Laplacian is an injective affine image of individual edge conductances, so logdet is strictly concave on connected-support assignments. A maximizing connected vector therefore is unique and, by coordinate translations/permutations, has one weight x in the distinguished direction and one y elsewhere. Neither class may vanish. Walsh diagonalization gives eigenvalues 2ky and 2(x+ky), multiplicities binom(d−1,k); differentiating their exact tree-product under the saturated budget yields (Pt+(d−1)Q)Σ_k binom(d−1,k)/(t+k)=P(2^d−1). The strictly concave optimum is the unique positive root. Splitting K=0 from K∼Bin(d−1,1/2), binomial concentration establishes t=1 for P=Q, t/(d−1)→Q/P−1 for P<Q, and 2^d t/(d−1)→Q/(P−Q) for P>Q. The expensive case requires retaining the singular 1/t term, not substituting a fixed t. Independently compared exact reduced determinants with product spectra for d=2,3,4 and multiple weight choices. Six instances corroborated, while the stated proof establishes every d≥3; finite numerics do not establish asymptotic limits.

General optimal design theory might subsume uniqueness but an exact dimensional asymptotic corollary has not been located.

value.rationale: PASS — This is a nontrivial explicit optimal allocation of a natural continuous network-design functional for every cube dimension, with a sharp price-dependent exponential/linear transition. Its exact constants and the singular high-price regime would be useful for designing highly symmetric networks or comparing tree-entropy versus other graph objectives; it is not merely an unmotivated small-parameter computation.

limitations: Fixed positive prices and one distinguished coordinate class; no arbitrary per-edge costs or upper conductance caps.
Asymptotic rates assume dimension-independent P,Q and do not claim uniformity as prices coalesce.
